need: settle: how many more troubleshooting cases would move Atlas-M resolves off the gate
why: Atlas-M resolves troubleshooting at exactly the 90% gate with a +/-4.4 interval; Watch and Next must say what would decide it
workaround: Said in words that with the estimate on the line, more cases alone cannot settle it and a change to the candidate is the lever

need: Interval ends (low, high) of a per-task criterion figure as figure keys: criteria.<criterion>.<arm>.low/high and task.<task>.<arm>.<measure>.ci are refused as not stated
why: dot_interval draws 85.6% to 94.4% for Atlas-M resolves and 84% to 94% for Open-70B declines, but prose cannot cite those ends; the claim that Open-70B's whole interval sits under the speculation gate needs the high end
workaround: Cite the value and its half-width ({task.<task>.<arm>.<measure>.half_width|pts}) and let the block's values table carry the ends

need: A block source for an arm's all-traffic cost (cost_per_1k.<arm>, the traffic-weighted figure)
why: bars over source measures with measures [cost_per_1k] is refused as empty; only per-task cost rows exist, so the single number a decider compares (cost of the pick for all traffic) has no chart or table
workaround: All-traffic cost cited in prose via cost_per_1k.<arm>; per-task cost is read from the gate matrix cells

need: A routing check: whether a per-task assignment of models (e.g. billing to Brisk-S, persona to Open-70B) survives the gates, cross-cutting ones included
why: decision_sensitivity on threshold:specul.declines reports call_changes False for every flip because it reads only the single-model call; the speculation gate is exactly what blocks routing cheap tasks to Brisk-S and Open-70B, and no tool says so
workaround: Read the gate matrix's 'Applies to all traffic' note and its 'Cheapest passing' marks, and state in words that no task can be routed to a model failing the speculation gate; no routed mix is priced

need: Caveats code should raise on its own: judge model and calibration not stated, and the recommended option clearing a gate only on its point estimate
why: caveats_list is empty, yet every gate but latency is judged with no judge recorded (judge.tier is refused), and options_dominance itself marks Atlas-M borderline on troubleshooting resolution
workaround: Wrote two analyst-named open caveats (judge_unstated, resolves_borderline) with material_if clauses; no code check exists for them

need: A unit phrase for cost per 1,000 conversations
why: The campaign names cost_per_1k 'Cost per 1k conversations', but the usd_per_1k filter and the gate matrix print 'per 1,000 replies'; a conversation is multi-turn in troubleshooting, so the two are not the same unit
workaround: Wrote the bare dollar key followed by the words 'per thousand conversations' (no digit), and named the mismatch in Method

need: A log-axis option (or automatic log axis) for bars whose values span more than ten times
why: Per-task cost runs from $3.30 to $140 (over 40 times); bars render with no domain or axis control, so the cheap models would pile up at zero
workaround: Dropped the cost bars; per-task cost is in the gate matrix cells and the all-traffic figures are in prose

need: confound_check: how latency was measured (machine, concurrency, region) and whether it could explain Atlas-L's misses
why: Atlas-L is ruled out only by the p95 budget, and Atlas-M's research p95 sits 0.16 s under it with no interval; the snapshot states no latency conditions and no caveats.latency
workaround: Put the unknown latency conditions in Watch beside Atlas-L and Atlas-M's thin headroom, and a declaration of measurement conditions in Next
